method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (vca-core.l4, with two regulative rules covering s 7(1A)-(1D) and (8)-(9) and the limits of ss 5(2), 5(3A), 6 and 6A) and one seat layer (vca-seat.l4) that restates no rule; awards are discretionary (s 5(1)), so the amount the Commissioner assesses is an input; no REFUSE (a s 4(1)(b) helper with no offence against them, an application determined before 15 December 2021, CPI figures that do not reach the year, and a lodgement before 20 April 2023 answer an explicit not-covered value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run vca-core.l4 ; l4 run vca-seat.l4 ; l4 run vca-cases.l4 ; l4 run vca-cases-maxima.l4
checks.result: 146 assertions satisfied (93 in vca-cases.l4, 53 in vca-cases-maxima.l4), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 6 #TRACEs with an expect line, all breaches (the applicant lodging a day late under s 7(1A) and under s 7(1B); the Commissioner awarding above the s 6A maximum, awarding where s 6(1)(a) excludes, and not determining within the s 7(8) period, twice), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. The Hobart CPI figures in vca-cases-maxima.l4 are hypothetical.

scope: Act s 2 (primary, secondary and related victim; offence; criminal conduct; injury including pregnancy; dependant); s 4(1)-(4) (death or injury from an offence or an excused act, or from assisting police; the heads open to each kind of victim: expenses, future medical, dental (primary only), psychological or counselling services, lost wages including while caring, pain and suffering, a related victim's dependency loss, costs of claiming) with s 4(1A)-(1B) (funeral expenses, conduct on or after 1 November 2015); s 5(2), (3A), (4), (9), (10) and s 40B (balance of probabilities; failure to help police; civil remedy, reported not deducted; law at lodgement; the greater of the maxima at lodgement and determination); s 6 (motor vehicle to MAIB, exemplary or aggravated damages, property, workers compensation head by head, Medicare and health funds); s 6A (class maxima per particular criminal conduct less amounts already awarded, the primary victim series maximum, the shared funeral maximum, future services above the cap); s 6B (deductions after the cap); s 7(1A)-(1D), (8), (9) (3 years from the offence, 3 years after turning 18, no limit for child sexual abuse, extensions as inputs, determination within 3 years); s 12; Regulations reg 4 (2021-22 maxima, indexed by the Hobart CPI as an input, never falling) and reg 5 (application contents, as a checklist). Out: Part 3 (property orders) and the victims fund (s 38); s 7A (recovery from the offender); procedure and publicity (s 7(2)-(7), (10), s 8); ss 2A, 3, 5(3), 5(5)-(7), 9, 10, 11, 40A, 41; reg 5(10) and Schedule 1. Read with subjects/au/tas/motor-accidents-liabilities-and-compensation-act-1973/ (s 6(1)(a)), subjects/au/tas/workers-rehabilitation-and-compensation-act-1988/ (s 6(1)(d)), subjects/au/health-insurance-act-1973/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (s 6(1)(e)(i)) and subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (s 17(2B)-(2C): an award here is not compensation under the Social Security Act); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the applicant: a primary, secondary or related victim of an offence, or a person who paid a primary victim's funeral expenses
